lessons.title: Return to a familiar completed action
lessons.gloss: retrieve a practice name, work, and a completed form

segments.instruction: Aman; kamm; kiitaa; YOU SAY: ਅਮਨ, ਕੰਮ, ਕੀਤਾ
segments.source: [YOU HEAR: *Aman; kamm; kiitaa*; YOU SAY: **ਅਮਨ · ਕੰਮ · ਕੀਤਾ**]

segments.text: ਕੰਮ is familiar “work.” ਕੀਤਾ is the familiar completed form in ਮੈਂ ਕੰਮ ਕੀਤਾ. In that old frame it agrees with the unmarked work object. Keep those pieces ready; the next lesson adds one small marker to a named person's completed action.

segments.instruction: the practice name; YOU SAY: ਅਮਨ
did, completed form; YOU SAY: ਕੀਤਾ

segments.text: Say only these familiar pieces. No new form is required yet.

lessons.title: A small marker after the agent
lessons.gloss: agent marker after a named person in this completed-action frame

needs: your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes or your hands for the steps that ask you to read, point, write or gesture. You can listen to everything else now. I will say so again when we reach them, but leave these sections until you have stopped: Grammar Lens: direct owner and Guided Practice.

segments.text: Recall the practice name ਅਮਨ, “work” ਕੰਮ, and the completed form ਕੀਤਾ.
ਨੇ — ne — marks the person who did the action in this frame ਅਮਨ ਨੇ ਕੰਮ ਕੀਤਾ — Aman ne kamm kiitaa — Aman did the work.

Put ਨੇ (ne) immediately after ਅਮਨ in this one third-person completed transitive action. The short marker points to the doer. Familiar ਕੀਤਾ still agrees with the unmarked masculine-singular object ਕੰਮ. Say the whole sentence once, then point to its doer, work, and action.

Punjabi University Patiala's lesson 14 shows a comparable completed-action pattern and warns that usage varies by sentence. This is a safe small example; not every past sentence takes ਨੇ (ne). The same written sound can also be a present-tense auxiliary at the end of a different sentence; that is not today's marker. We do not generalise beyond this named-agent, third-person frame.

segments.instruction: Aman ne kamm kiitaa; YOU SAY: ਅਮਨ ਨੇ ਕੰਮ ਕੀਤਾ

lessons.title: ਨੇ (ne)
lessons.gloss: retrieve the agent marker by sound, meaning, and script

segments.text: Remember the tiny marker immediately after ਅਮਨ in the completed-action sentence.

segments.instruction: ne, after the doer; YOU SAY: ਨੇ
segments.source: [YOU HEAR: *ne, after the doer*; YOU SAY: **ਨੇ**]

segments.instruction: cover the model and write ਨੇ (ne) once

segments.text: If it does not come yet, look back at the model and try again. The two visible pieces are familiar; the new work is where this whole marker sits.
Say where the marker belongs: after the named doer in today's completed-action frame.

You can listen to everything else now. I will say so again when we reach them, but leave these sections until you have stopped: Guided Practice and Wrap-up Recall.

segments.text: Say ਅਮਨ, then the new marker ਨੇ (ne). Recall ਕੰਮ ਕੀਤਾ from the earlier completed-action chapter.
ਅਮਨ ਨੇ ਕੰਮ ਕੀਤਾ — Aman ne kamm kiitaa — Aman did the work.
Read left to right: named doer, small agent marker, work object, completed action. Keep this one frame; do not use it to guess a rule for every past sentence.
